requirements: Edit `src/relay/mission/julius/julius-memory-trust.ts` so no exported function throws `memory_trust_not_implemented`. Keep every exported name, signature and type exactly as declared.

AUTO-GENERATE IS ALLOWED, AUTO-TRUST IS NOT. `admitJuliusMemoryCandidate` always admits at trust `UNVERIFIED`, whatever `requestedTrust` asks for. A caller requesting more is NOT refused for that reason — it is admitted at `UNVERIFIED`.

`admitJuliusMemoryCandidate` refuses (returns `{ outcome: 'REFUSED', reasonCode }`) a claim with an empty or blank `claimId`, `entryId` or `assertedBy`, or a `provenance` outside the declared vocabulary.

`promoteJuliusMemoryClaim` is verification-gated. Promotion to `VERIFIED` requires at least one evidence reference of kind `REVIEW` or `FINDING`, and the promoting authority `by` must not equal the claim's own `assertedBy`: a claim cannot verify itself.
Promotion to `APPROVED` requires at least one evidence reference of kind `DECISION`. Promotion to `SUPPORTED` requires at least one evidence reference of any kind that the asserter did not supply.
A claim whose trust is `CONTRADICTED` or `SUPERSEDED` can never be promoted again; `promoteJuliusMemoryClaim` refuses it.

`contradictJuliusMemoryClaims(a, b, at)` records the conflict on BOTH claims — each claim's `contradicts` gains the other's `claimId` — and neither claim is deleted. Both become `CONTRADICTED`, EXCEPT that a claim already at `APPROVED` keeps `APPROVED`: an adopted claim is not demoted by a bare assertion.

`supersedeJuliusMemoryClaim(existing, replacement, at)` marks `existing` as `SUPERSEDED` and sets the replacement's `supersedes` to the existing `claimId`. It refuses when the two claims are about different `entryId`s, and refuses a claim superseding itself.

`promoteJuliusMemoryClaim` only ever RAISES standing, in the ordering `UNVERIFIED < SUPPORTED < VERIFIED < APPROVED`. A target at or below the claim's current standing is refused, and `CONTRADICTED` and `SUPERSEDED` are never promotion targets — those are reached by `contradictJuliusMemoryClaims` and `supersedeJuliusMemoryClaim`, which record why.

`retrieveTrustedJuliusMemory(claims, { minimumTrust, role })` returns only claims whose trust is at or above `minimumTrust` in the declared ordering `UNVERIFIED < SUPPORTED < VERIFIED < APPROVED`, and NEVER returns a claim whose trust is `CONTRADICTED` or `SUPERSEDED`, whatever standing it once had.
Every function is pure: it must not mutate any argument. A claim handed in comes back unchanged, and results are new objects.

acceptanceCriteria.text: No exported function in `julius-memory-trust.ts` throws `memory_trust_not_implemented`, and every exported name, signature and type is unchanged.
`admitJuliusMemoryCandidate` admits at `UNVERIFIED` for every possible `requestedTrust`, including `APPROVED` — auto-generation is allowed, auto-trust is not.
A candidate with a blank `claimId`, `entryId` or `assertedBy`, or a provenance outside the vocabulary, is REFUSED rather than admitted.

Promotion to `VERIFIED` requires `REVIEW` or `FINDING` evidence AND an authority different from the claim's own `assertedBy`; a claim cannot verify itself, and promotion with no evidence or the wrong evidence kind is refused.
A `CONTRADICTED` or `SUPERSEDED` claim is never promoted again.
Contradiction records the conflict on both claims and deletes neither; an `APPROVED` claim is not demoted by a conflicting bare assertion, which itself becomes `CONTRADICTED`.
Supersession marks the existing claim `SUPERSEDED` and links the replacement's `supersedes`, and refuses a different `entryId` or a claim superseding itself.

Promotion only raises standing: a target at or below the claim's current trust is refused, and `CONTRADICTED`/`SUPERSEDED` are never promotion targets — so an `APPROVED` claim can never be quietly returned to `UNVERIFIED`.
Retrieval honours the trust ordering and never returns a `CONTRADICTED` or `SUPERSEDED` claim, whatever standing it once had.
No function mutates an argument; a claim handed in comes back unchanged.
The declared test command exits zero against the unmodified specification test.
